name: write_symbols
description: Batch write primitive (P4). Implicit all_or_nothing transaction: multiple symbol/patch writes across files commit together or roll back together (compensation transaction + journal, not FS-level atomic). Files are grouped, locked in path-sorted order (deadlock-safe), each file written once atomically, reindexed once after write. Same-file multi-symbol edits are relocated by line delta (no stale ranges). Returns txn_id + per-item status + full batch diff + undo token. Always read_symbol each target first to obtain base_version (required for the first write of each file). For multi-file refactors (e.g. rename login to authenticate across 3 files) use this instead of N×write_symbol. dry_run supported. Do not use edit_transaction for batch symbol edits.

workspace_dir.description: REQUIRED: Absolute path to the project root directory.

symbol_id.description: Stable symbol id (preferred). Read it from read_symbol output.

locator.description: Symbol locator. Omit for file-level patch.

content.description: New content. For replace_symbol: full new symbol (boundary=full) or new body (boundary=body). For patch: new_string.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace (must be unique)

boundary.description: full (default) or body (keep signature, replace rest)

base_version.description: Version object from read_symbol. Required for the first write of each file (unless allow_unsafe_no_base). Later writes in the same file are checked at symbol level.

writes.description: REQUIRED: Array of writes. Grouped by file internally.

all_or_nothing.description: Default true: any failure rolls back all written files (compensation + journal). Set false for best_effort.

dry_run.description: Validate and produce diffs without writing (default false)

allow_unsafe_no_base.description: Bypass base_version requirement for all writes (audited).

block_on_validation_error.description: Block batch if validation fails (default false)

writes.content:
def login(self, username, password):
    return self._hash(username, password)
